A state of maximum emergency has been declared in Gaza after a rainstorm flooded about 70,000 tents housing displaced Palestinians, causing at least five deaths and overwhelming rescue services.  The first storm of the second winter since the ceasefire of 2024 came last weekend, prompting warnings of a worsening humanitarian situation for hundreds of thousands of displaced people living in temporary camps, lacking adequate protection from rain and wind.  Tents usually supplied by emergency charities have been held by the Israeli blockade outside the camps, according to the charity ShelterBox.  “We are living in a truly tragic reality,” says Thaer Abu Hamad, a displaced person from Beit Lahia. “We need someone to look upon us with mercy."

“Gen0cide Joe!” “Bl00d on your hands!” That’s what pro-Palestinian protesters shouted at former President Joe Biden in Dublin on Tuesday, according to the Telegraph and NBC News. Some demonstrators also threw milk and other objects toward the former president as he departed Trinity College, where he and former First Lady Jill Biden had attended an event honoring their son, Hunter Biden. He received the Gold Medal for Outstanding Contribution to Public Discourse from the university’s College Historical Society. Irish police said Wednesday that three men had been arrested in connection with the incident, although two of them were released without being charged. Biden has long been criticized for how he handled Israel’s war with Palestine. His administration provided Israel with billions of dollars in military assistance, despite growing outrage over civilian casualties in Gaza. Ireland has some of the strongest pro-Palestinian public sentiment in the Western world, with many citizens drawing parallels between Palestinians’ experiences under Israeli occupation and Ireland’s own history under British colonial rule. #biden #israel #palestine #protest #ireland
